about: The single source for every listed vocabulary word. The key is the word's permanent id (saves and scenes use it; never rename, add an alias instead). 'text' gives its display text in every language of data/languages.json; for Spanish one primary Mexican Spanish translation with its article (' / ' only separates masculine/feminine forms of a person, as in 'el niño / la niña', the two senses of 'fish', or the approved synonyms noted on 'hair'). Optional 'forms' gives per-language grammar data, needed only by words that fill a {slot:form} in data/phrases.json (shapes: scripts/language/rules_<code>.gd). 'category' is one of 'categories' (each value is the rule for what belongs there); optional prefab_size for generated learning prefabs, optional note, optional sold_in. 'aliases' maps old or synonym keys to a word. Numbers, money amounts and dates are generated by the language rules modules, not listed here. Edit here only; run python3 tools/word_data.py to validate and re-format, and godot --headless --path . --script res://tools/language_check.gd to check languages. See docs/guides/ARCHITECTURE_REVIEW_PART1.md#vocabulary-data-procedure.

categories.Food & Drink: Things you eat or drink, meals, and the menus and recipes that list them.
categories.Kitchen & Dining: Cookware, tableware and anything used to prepare, serve or eat food.
categories.Furniture: Things you sit, sleep, work or store things on or in, at home or in public buildings.
categories.Around the House: Small household objects, textiles, decorations and lighting that are not furniture.
categories.Electronics & Appliances: Anything that plugs in or runs on batteries: devices, screens and household machines.
categories.Places & Rooms: Buildings, shops, rooms and named areas you can go to.
categories.Building Parts: Fixed parts of a building: walls, doors, windows, floors, plumbing and fittings.
categories.Streets & Town: Outdoor public things: roads, sidewalks, signs, bridges and street furniture.
categories.Vehicles: Things that carry people or goods, and their parts.
categories.Travel: Trips and airports: travel documents, luggage, and the counters, checkpoints and displays of an airport.
categories.Countries: Countries of the world as travel destinations: proper names, written without an article (airport flight game, 5 Nov 2026).
categories.Shopping & Money: Paying, money, prices, tickets and the counters and displays of shops and banks.
categories.School & Arts: Books, paper, school supplies, school subjects, art and music.
categories.Health & Body: The body, medical care and equipment, and personal hygiene.
categories.Clothing: Clothes, shoes and things you wear or carry on your body.
categories.Sports & Play: Sports equipment, toys, playground items and party games.
categories.Family: Relatives and partners, and the words for comparing ages (older, younger).
categories.Nature: Plants, trees, weather, landscape and natural materials.
categories.Time & Directions: Times of day, days, months, words for order in time (before, after), and directions or positions.
categories.Actions: Verbs: things you do, shown in the infinitive (to put, to push, to find).
categories.Colors & Descriptions: Colors, shapes and words that describe what things and people are like: size, weight, height, hair, and how they look, feel and sound.

apple pie.note: Mexican; Spain says la tarta de manzana.

beef.note: Mexican; Spain says la carne de ternera.

text.es: la carne de res con verduras

lamb.note: The meat; the young animal is also el cordero.

orange juice.note: Mexican; Spain says el zumo de naranja.

cardboard box.note: la caja alone is also the checkout counter (its own word).

container.note: An open plastic storage bin in the warehouse; things go dentro del contenedor.

ladder.note: a ladder; stairs are las escaleras

shower curtain.note: Taught by the welcome tutorial at the family bathtub's curtain (home_furnishing.gd); the first friend hides behind it. No node carries this word.

electrical box.note: the wall-mounted box outside the home (docs/guides/ELECTRICAL_BOX.md)

statue.note: The Washington statue in the monument plaza (base step statue_word, 12 Nov 2026); taught in the welcome tutorial. Its card reads 'statue of George Washington' (user, 17 Nov 2026); the key stays statue.

boarding gate.note: Mexican airports say sala (SALA A1); la puerta is already the word for door.

china.note: The country; the word for porcelain is not listed.

text.es: el puesto de frutas y verduras

hair.note: el pelo and el cabello are synonyms for the same object (user request, 31 Oct 2026); an approved exception to one translation per word.

堂兄弟姐妹 / 表兄弟姐妹

older.note: Comparing people's ages (mi hermano mayor). 'El mayor' (the oldest) is built in phrases, not a separate word.

text.zh: 伯父 / 叔叔 / 舅父 / 姑丈 / 姨丈

younger.note: Comparing people's ages (mi hermana menor). 'El menor' (the youngest) is built in phrases, not a separate word.

hay.note: hay bales in the barn; everyday Mexican word (el heno is the textbook term)

stone.note: A small stone you can hold; a big rock is la roca.

half past.note: a las ocho y media. Quarter past / quarter to were left out by user decision (5 Nov 2026).

last night.note: anoche: 20:00 yesterday to 04:59 today in the flight game.

o'clock.note: Clock times: a las ocho en punto. Taught on the airport clock poster; flight times are generated (flight game).

on.note: sobre: on, or above; encima de is on top of.

this afternoon.note: esta tarde runs until 19:59 in the flight game; esta noche starts at 20:00.

to arrive.note: Its forms llegó / llega / va a llegar appear in the flight game's arrival sentences (data/phrases.json group 'flight', 8 Nov 2026); tracked when the verb decides the answer.

to be.note: estar: where something is or how it is (location or state), not ser.

to depart.note: Its forms salió / sale / va a salir appear in the flight game's sentences (data/phrases.json group 'flight').

to leave.note: To leave something somewhere, put it down; not to leave a place.

to remove.note: To take something off or away from a place.

to squeeze.note: To press something with your hand to feel if it is hard or soft (the police evidence game's Apretar tool, 8 Nov 2026).

brown.note: Things (a brown box, 8 Nov 2026, Warehouse Worker); hair and eyes are brown (hair). Same form for masculine and feminine; Mexico also says café.

brown (hair).note: Hair and eye colour; feminine castaña. Other brown things are café or marrón.

circle.note: Mystery Doors minigame (9 Nov 2026): taught by the Mystery House hall poster; a door shows it.

cold.note: Feminine fría. Chinese: Hong Kong 凍 (cold food and drinks).

fizzy.note: Drinks with bubbles; without them: sin gas.

hot.note: Temperature; spicy food is picante (English hot can mean either).

light (weight).note: Feminine ligera. The opposite of heavy; a lamp's light is the word light (la luz).

long.note: Feminine larga. False friend: largo means long, not large.

loud.note: A loud sound is un sonido fuerte; fuerte also means strong.

medium.note: A size between big and small (the medium box, 8 Nov 2026, Warehouse Worker); feminine mediana.

orange (color).note: The colour; the same for masculine and feminine. The fruit is la naranja.

pink.note: The same for masculine and feminine; Mexico also says rosado.

short (height).note: Feminine baja. For people's height; a short rope is corto.

short (length).note: Feminine corta. For length (hair, rope); a short person is bajo.

small.note: Feminine pequeña; Mexico also says chico.

soft.note: Feminine blanda; Mexico also says suave.

sour.note: Feminine ácida; Mexico also says agrio.

spicy.note: Hot as in chili; hot temperature is caliente.

square.note: Mystery Doors minigame (9 Nov 2026): taught by the Mystery House hall poster; a door shows it. The shape; a town square is la plaza.

star.note: Mystery Doors minigame (9 Nov 2026): taught by the Mystery House hall poster; a door shows it. The shape (Chinese 星形); a star in the sky is also la estrella.

sweet.note: Same form for masculine and feminine. Restaurant game taste word (6 Nov 2026).

triangle.note: Mystery Doors minigame (9 Nov 2026): taught by the Mystery House hall poster; a door shows it.

wet.note: Feminine mojada; used with estar (está mojado).
